# QUESTIONS — closed (client answered on Sept. 28, 2026); remaining unknowns flagged

The client has answered the dispositive questions and states she has no additional information. Answered questions are **not** re-asked below. Remaining unknowns are recorded as flagged gaps with their effect, and most are things we must obtain from records rather than from the client.

## Answered (the removal question is resolved)

| Topic | Client's answer | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| LLC members and domiciles | Noor Haddad 65%, lives Portland OR; **Caleb Sorensen 35%, lives Seattle (Ballard)**; only two members | LLC is a citizen of **Washington and Oregon** (*Johnson*); plaintiff is a Washington citizen → no complete diversity (§ 1332(a)(1)) and the forum-defendant rule applies (§ 1441(b)(2)). **Removal unavailable — do not file.** |
| Date CSC received/forwarded the papers | Emailed scans **Sept. 11, 2026** to an old Gmail account; found Sun. night, Sept. 27 | Confirms Sept. 11 as the trigger for both the state answer (Oct. 1) and the § 1446(b)(1) clock (Oct. 13, now moot). No time can be bought with the "old inbox" point |
| Disputed deliveries | Three, **March–April 2026**, **about $26,000**; photos and emails exist; invoices never paid | Setoff/defense for ~$26,000; but leaves **~$84,916.40** of the pleaded $110,916.40 unpaid and unexplained on her own account |
| Remaining questions | "no additional information" | No further client questions will be sent; the gaps below are flagged instead |

## Client query, Sept. 28 — answered in the memo, not left open

**Q (Noor):** "My friend was really sure — Delaware LLC vs Washington corporation is textbook diversity. Caleb being in Seattle shouldn't matter, the company isn't him. Are you sure we can't remove?"

**A:** Yes. His rule is 28 U.S.C. § 1332(c)(1) — incorporation state plus principal place of business — and per the library it "applies to corporations." Harbor Street is an LLC, an unincorporated association, so the corporate test "does **not** apply"; instead it "is a citizen of every state of which its owners/members are citizens" (*Johnson v. Columbia Properties Anchorage, LP*, 437 F.3d 894, 899 (9th Cir. 2006): "like a partnership, an LLC is a citizen of every state of which its owners/members are citizens"; *Carden v. Arkoma Associates*, 494 U.S. 185 (1990)). Delaware organization is not a citizenship for an LLC, so the defendant is a **Washington** (Caleb) and Oregon (Noor) citizen against a Washington plaintiff — no complete diversity — and the forum-defendant rule (§ 1441(b)(2)) bars it independently. A removed case would go to W.D. Wash. under § 1441(a), not Delaware, and § 1447(c) adds remand-plus-fees risk. Full walk-through, including the corporation-vs-LLC comparison table: `memo.md` § 5.6.

**Narrow evidence request (the only fact that could change the answer):** the test is **domicile**, not residence. If facts already exist that contradict Washington domicile for Caleb — Oregon driver's license, Oregon voter registration, Oregon tax filing, an unbroken Oregon lease — send them and the analysis will be re-run; on that scenario the LLC would be an Oregon-only citizen and the `if_removed` dates (answer Oct. 7; scheduling order Nov. 30; Rule 26(f) conference Nov. 9) would become live. Do not solicit a favorable characterization from Caleb, and do not let this question delay the **Oct. 1** answer.

## Remaining unknowns — flagged explicitly

1. **Operating agreement and membership ledger not produced.** Roster is the client's word (65/35, two members). Needed for: the 12% contract interest rate, § 14 fee clause, risk-of-loss terms for the May 19, 2026 butter incident, and any forum-selection/arbitration/choice-of-law clause. Effect on removal: none (Caleb alone is fatal); a larger roster would only reinforce "no removal."
2. **Caleb Sorensen: domicile vs. residence.** "Lives in Seattle (Ballard)" shows residence; *Johnson* measures domicile. This is the **only** fact that could flip the removal answer — an Oregon-domiciled Caleb would make the LLC an Oregon-only citizen and open removal — but nothing reported supports it, the removing party carries the risk of being wrong, and § 1447(c) makes a wrong guess expensive. Treated as Washington citizenship; flagged, not pursued by asking him to characterize his own ties.
3. **Caleb's role on May 19, 2026.** Complaint ¶ 6 pleads an "employee"; the client calls him a "partner" who signed for deliveries. Matters to the negligence claim ($18,240) and to the jury story; irrelevant to diversity, since he is a member either way.
4. **Invoice-level reconciliation.** Whether the ~$26,000 of disputed invoices sits inside the $110,916.40 balance, and which invoice numbers they are ($26,000 is the client's approximation). Complaint pleads deliveries "Between January and July 2026" totaling $142,316.40 but does not itemize. **Does not reconcile from the file — left open.**
5. **The residual ~$84,916.40.** No stated reason it is unpaid ($110,916.40 − $26,000). Need Harbor Street's own AR ledger.
6. **Consequential damages** from the short/spoiled deliveries (lost sales, cover purchases, labor) — needed to decide whether to plead a counterclaim or only a setoff. Unknown.
7. **Insurance** for the negligence claim and whether a carrier has been noticed. Unknown.
8. **Whether anything preceded the Sept. 11 service** (earlier attempt, service on a Washington registered agent). Nothing in the documents suggests it; all dates are computed from Sept. 11, 2026.
9. **Post-answer Washington deadlines** (case setting, discovery cut-offs, trial setting) — **not computable from the closed library**, which contains only CR 4, 6, 12, and 55 excerpts. Will not be guessed.
10. **Whether a pre-answer CR 12(b) motion would extend the Oct. 1 answer date, and whether we may still file a jury demand** — not in the library; confirm locally before relying on either. Do not let either question delay the answer.

facts.answer: Yes — Caleb Sorensen owns 35% of the LLC. He lives in Seattle (Ballard). I own 65% and live in Portland. We're the only two members.
CSC emailed the scans on the 11th to our old Gmail. Nobody checks it. I found them Sunday night.
Nobody has filed anything for us. We don't have a Washington lawyer.
Three deliveries in March–April were short or spoiled, about $26k worth. I have photos and emails. I never paid those invoices.
